title: Adaptive burst-handshake for active-active gateway failover (stream-safe traffic shifting)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: our hosted API gateways currently perform bulk regional traffic shifts that assume idempotent, short-lived requests. Streaming sessions (chat streaming, partial responses) and long-lived session affinity break during aggressive active-active failover, producing user-facing disconnects, duplicate tokens, and KV-cache inconsistency. This ticket defines and implements an "adaptive burst-handshake" protocol: a light-weight pre-shift probe + per-session handshake that enables safe, progressive traffic shifting across active regions while preserving stream continuity, minimizing error surface, and respecting token/KV cache correctness.

Goals:
- Shift traffic between regions in active-active without dropping streaming sessions or returning inconsistent generation state.
- Keep failover latency within SLOs: P99 request completion for control plane ops <= 250ms, streaming resume latency <= 800ms with <1% increased 4xx/5xx on the receiving region during shift.
- Provide circuit-breaker knobs and load-shedding thresholds to prevent cascade during regional congestion.
- Expose observability and automated rollback on key signals (session error ratio, kv-mismatch rate, model tail latency).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change model checkpoint replication or persistent datastore HA topology. It focuses on ephemeral session handoff, KV prefix sync for serving caches, and gateway traffic shaping logic.

Context and background: we learned from Incident I-2026-03-edgefail that blunt traffic drains caused ~2.3% streaming session reconnects and exposed a race where two regions served overlapping requests with divergent KV caches. Existing active-active steering is region-level and stateless; streaming semantics require session-awareness and a short-lived handshake to establish resume tokens and validate KV prefixes.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway supports a pre-shift probe API that validates target region readiness (capacity, model-variant compatibility, KV prefix hash) and returns a shift-token for each session to be moved.

Streaming clients can request a resume token via the handshake; resumed streams reconnect to the target region and retrieve a validated KV prefix version. Resume latency (median) <= 350ms, P95 <= 650ms in controlled canary.

Circuit-breaker integrated: when target region p95 generation latency or error-rate exceeds configured thresholds, handshake requests are rejected with explicit 'defer' reasons and are surfaceable in rollouts dashboard.

Load-shedding policy: burst-level shed decisions applied at shard-level using short-term QPS and queue depth with clear metrics; shed events trigger fallback to cached-response or client-guidance path with graceful messaging.

Automated progressive shift playbook implemented: canary phases 1/5/25/50/100 with automatic halt on any of the three signals crossing thresholds (session error ratio, kv-mismatch rate, model-tail-latency).

End-to-end e2e tests for sessionful shift, including: content-consistency (no duplicated tokens), KV-prefix mismatch detection, and stream-resume correctness under jitter and packet loss simulated conditions.
implementation_plan: Spec handshake protocol and message format (preflight probe, shift-token, resume-token, kv-prefix-hash). -> Confluence doc link.
Add gateway control plane endpoint `/v1/gateway/preflight` that validates region compatibility and emits shift-tokens; implement short TTL (30s) for tokens.

Implement session coordinator in gateway edge to orchestrate per-session handover: stepwise transition (probe -> freeze inbound KV updates -> drain small in-flight window -> apply token on target -> resume).

KV prefix validation: lightweight hash + epoch number included in preflight; if mismatch, target region will pull latest ephemeral cache entries via a prioritized KV sync task before accepting resume.
Circuit-breaker hooks: p95 latency, error-rate, queue-depth; integrate with existing runtime circuit controller and allow per-customer overrides.
Load-shedding integration: when target is overloaded, return instructive 429 with 'retry-after' and optional short cached snippet; ensure SDKs can surface friendly message to product teams.
Observability: add Grafana panels for handshake success rate, resume latency histogram, kv-prefix-mismatch rate, per-canary-step failure reasons. Add SLO alerting (on-call alerts + runbook).
Testing: unit tests, integration tests with streaming harness, staged canary rollout across two low-traffic regions, blue-green fallback tests, and chaos injection to validate rollback triggers.
risk_and_mitigation: Race window where both regions accept writes for a session -> Mitigation: short freeze window and append-only sequence numbers during handoff; if a mismatch is detected, prefer canonical sequence from origin region and apply compensating requests.
Handshake tokens leaked/used incorrectly -> Mitigation: tokens are single-use, short TTL, signed and include origin region signature; audit logs emitted for token issuance/use.

Increased control-plane overhead under many concurrent handoffs -> Mitigation: throttle preflight probes per customer and aggregate probes when doing bulk shifts; use probabilistic sampling for very large shifts.

False-positive kv-prefix mismatches due to transient cache eviction -> Mitigation: accept one tolerant mismatch and trigger on-demand prioritized sync rather than immediate abort for lower-impact sessions.
observability_requirements: Metrics: handshake_requests_total, handshake_success_total, handshake_failure_by_reason, resume_latency_ms_bucketed, kv_prefix_mismatch_count, shed_events_total, shed_reasons.
Dashboards: per-region handshake health, per-customer error ratio during shift, circuit-breaker state timeline per region.
Logs: structured audit events for token issuance/usage, KV-sync jobs kicked off, and session freeze/drain timestamps.
Alerts: P1 when handshake_success_rate < 98% over 5m during rollout, P2 when kv_prefix_mismatch_rate increases >0.2% over baseline.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit and integration tests in CI; internal staging environment exercise with synthetic load (3x expected).
Stage 1 (Canary 1%): enable for a small customer cohort across two non-critical regions; observe metrics for 4 hours before progressing.
Stage 2 (Canary 5%): expand cohort; run live traffic pairing with active chaos runner to simulate packet loss and 200ms RTTs.
Stage 3 (Canary 25%): enable across more regions with automated rollback on signals (see acceptance criteria).
Stage 4 (General): full rollout with telemetry retention increased for 72h and on-call ready with documented runbook.
